goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — The compatibility wrapper omits the `-moz-box-align` counterpart used by `flexbox()` but emits nonexistent `-ms-align-items`, so its prefix contract is both incomplete and partly dead.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies issues in the `@mixin align-items` at line 117. Looking at the diff: (1) The `flexbox()` mixin includes `-moz-box` prefix but `align-items()` does not include `-moz-box-align`, which is inconsistent. (2) The mixin includes `-ms-align-items` which is not a valid CSS property - the correct IE10 flexbox property would be `-ms-flex-align` (which is already included). So `-ms-align-items` is indeed dead/invalid code. This is a real defect in the cross-browser compatibility implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss:30 — This global order rule only works because `header.scss` independently makes its parent flex, creating an implicit cross-file layout dependency.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a cross-file dependency. In topic.scss line 30, `@include order(2)` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` CSS property only works when the parent element is a flex container. Looking at header.scss, the `.contents` class (which would be the parent) gets `@include flexbox()` added. This creates an implicit dependency where topic.scss's order rule relies on header.scss making the parent a flex container. This is a valid architectural concern about maintainability - if someone modifies header.scss without knowing about this dependency, the layout could break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:14 — The float-to-flex layout change has no visual or responsive regression coverage for item ordering and overflow at narrow widths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a significant layout change from float-based to flexbox-based layout in header.scss. The finding correctly identifies that this architectural change (removing 'float: left' from .title, removing 'float: right' from .panel, adding flexbox with order properties) could affect visual rendering and responsive behavior. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for a layout refactor, though the diff itself cannot show whether such tests exist elsewhere. The concern is specific and grounded in the actual code changes.
